title: 想走但唔想失禮
scenario: Two coworkers at the end of a long meeting, one needs to leave but doesnʼt want to be rude (A1)

sourceNotes: The particle 晒 (saai3) adds emphasis or completeness to verbs and adjectives: 多謝晒 (do1 ze6 saai3) = "thank you very much," 買晒 (maai5 saai3) = "bought everything." It intensifies the meaning. 走先 (zau2 sin1) literally means "leave first" and is the standard colloquial expression for departing before others. Itʼs more natural than saying 我先走 (Mandarin word order). The pattern 開咗...鐘 (hoi1 zo2...zung1) expresses duration: 開咗三個鐘 (hoi1 zo2 saam1 go3 zung1) = "has been going on for three hours." This uses the perfective aspect marker 咗 (zo2) with the duration after the verb. 仔女 (zai2 neoi5) literally means "sons and daughters" but is the standard term for "children" in general, regardless of gender composition. 剩返 (zing6 faan1) means "remaining/left over" and combines two verbs to indicate whatʼs left: 剩返幾個人 (zing6 faan1 gei2 go3 jan4) = "a few people left." Confidence Level: High
